introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination / Technical and Vocational Education Examination. Computer Science 2 (0595), ORDINARY / INTERMEDIATE LEVELS, June 2020. Duration: two hours.**

Answer any FIVE questions. All questions carry 20 marks each. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and phones are NOT allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Table 1 is used to register student's information in a certain school.

**Table 1**

| ADMISSION NUMBER | NAME OF STUDENT | DATE OF BIRTH | CLASS | FEES PAID |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|  |  |  |  |  |
|  |  |  |  |  |

(i) What do you understand by the term key field? (2 marks)

(ii) Which of the fields in Table 1 is suitable to used as a key field? Give a reason for your answer. (2 marks)

(iii) Give appropriate data types for the entries in the following fields: ADMISSION NUMBER, NAME OF STUDENT, DATE OF BIRTH, CLASS. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Key field (2 marks).** A key field (primary key) is a field whose value is **different for every record** of the table and is never left empty, so it identifies each record uniquely. It is used to find a particular record quickly, to avoid duplicate records and to link the table to other tables.

**(ii) Suitable key field (2 marks).** The field **ADMISSION NUMBER**. Reason: every student receives their own admission number, so no two students share it, whereas names, dates of birth, classes and fees paid can be the same for several students.

**(iii) Data types (4 marks).**

| Field | Suitable data type | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| ADMISSION NUMBER | Text (a Number type is also accepted if it contains digits only) | An identifier, not used in calculations; it may contain letters or leading zeros |
| NAME OF STUDENT | Text | Letters and spaces |
| DATE OF BIRTH | Date/Time | A calendar date |
| CLASS | Text | For example "Form 5" or "Lower Sixth" |

questions.enonce_markdown:
Briefly explain what you understand by each of the following:

(i) Bootstrap (2 marks)

(ii) Ergonomics (2 marks)

(iv) A milestone in project management (2 marks)

(v) A biometric system (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Bootstrap (2 marks).** The bootstrap (or boot) program is a small program stored permanently in the ROM of the computer. When the computer is switched on it starts first, checks that the hardware works, and then loads the operating system from the disk into the main memory (RAM) so that the computer can be used. This process is called booting.

**(ii) Ergonomics (2 marks).** Ergonomics is the study of how to design equipment and the working environment so that they fit the people who use them, for comfort, efficiency, health and safety. In computing it covers, for example, an adjustable chair, a screen at eye level, a well-placed keyboard and good lighting, to avoid back pain, eye strain and repetitive strain injury.

**(iv) A milestone in project management (2 marks).** A milestone is an important point or event in the life of a project that marks the completion of a major stage or deliverable (for example "requirements approved" or "system delivered"). It takes no time itself and is used to check the progress of the project against the plan.

**(v) A biometric system (2 marks).** A biometric system identifies or checks a person using a unique physical or behavioural characteristic, for example fingerprint, face, iris or voice. A sensor captures the characteristic and the system compares it with the template stored earlier. It is used for access control and for attendance.

questions.enonce_markdown: Distinguish briefly between data verification and data validation. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Data verification (2 marks)** is the check that the data entered into the computer is **exactly the same as the original source** (it has been copied accurately), for example by entering the data twice and comparing the two entries, or by proofreading it against the source document. It does not tell whether the data is sensible.

**Data validation (2 marks)** is the automatic check made by the program that the data entered is **reasonable and acceptable** according to rules, for example a range check (a mark must be between 0 and 20), a type check (digits only), a length check or a presence check. It does not prove that the data is correct: a wrongly typed age of 25 instead of 52 passes a range check.
